messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: NO namespace/file-level includes
parts:
Please don't put includes at the namespace or
file level. It pollutes the entire namespace.

Daniel and I are taking one set of these out of
lkj_corr.hpp right now and will try to hunt down any
others, but there are a lot of using statements in
Stan.

Does anyone know another way to hunt for spurious
includes?

- Bob

Getting rid of spurious includes is good, too.
We should run this again and clean up now that Daniel's
refactored so much of the math lib.

Attached is the result of

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp/llvm/build/bin$ export CFLAGS="-I /opt/stan/src -I /opt/stan/lib/eigen_3.1.2/ -I /opt/stan/lib/boost_1.53.0/ -Wall -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS"

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp/llvm/build/bin$ find /opt/stan/src/stan -name '*.hpp' -print0 | parallel -0 -j7 ./include-what-you-use $CFLAGS {} "2>" {}_iwyu.txt

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp/llvm/build/bin$ cd /opt/stan/src/stan

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan/src/stan$ find . -name '*_iwyu.txt' -print0 | xargs -0 tar -rf /tmp/iwyu.tar

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan/src/stan$ gzip /tmp/iwyu.tar

Thus, the foo.hpp_iwyu.txt files that say what should and should not be included in foo.hpp can be unzipped relative to $STAN_HOME/src/stan but you might want to instead do

cd /tmp
mkdir -p STAN_TEMP/src/stan
cd STAN_TEMP/src/stan
tar -xvf /path/to/iwyu.tar.gz .

Ben


Ben

This comes from us extending Eigen's base type with an EigenDenseMatrixPlugin so we can exchange std::vector and Eigen (row-)vectors and use appropriate types for indexing.

Daniel

I can do it again anytime, but according to the include-what-you-use principle, something like

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ cat src/stan.hpp
#ifndef STAN_HPP
#define STAN_HPP

// #include "stan/gm.hpp"
#include "stan/io.hpp"
#include "stan/memory.hpp"
#include "stan/mcmc.hpp"
#include "stan/meta.hpp"
#include "stan/model.hpp"
#include "stan/prob.hpp"
#include "stan/version.hpp"

#endif

should just be deleted because whatever might need any of the above .hpp files should be #including it directly rather than #including <stan.hpp> and pulling in those things indirectly. That said, I don't know if it is possible to fully adhere to the include-what-you-use principle, particularly with the model header. I did a model once before at

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-dev/q977l_VE2Ls/0spLJnlceXIJ

and it suggested a lot of changes, but I don't know if it is possible to make the parser sophisticated enough to do that for an arbitrary model.

Ben

On Monday, April 15, 2013 2:18:56 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Indexes in Eigen are ints :-(  So as not to
get gripes from the compiler about signed/unsigned
assignments, we need to use the typedefs in polymorphic
code.

I was pretty sure that got changed for Eigen 3.0
http://listengine.tuxfamily.org/lists.tuxfamily.org/eigen/2010/05/msg00161.html

It can be set:
http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox-devel/classEigen_1_1DenseBase.html#a4d4873e91be950c079f067fa97fd5c40

which refers to
http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox-devel/TopicPreprocessorDirectives.html

which says:
EIGEN_DEFAULT_DENSE_INDEX_TYPE - the type for column and row indices in matrices, vectors and array (DenseBase::Index). Set to std::ptrdiff_t by default.

So, I was wrong about remembering it being a size_t, and it is still signed. My commit should be reverted, but I'm still not sure why it was failing before.

Ben
